dossier.scp_unleashed.131.title: The Eye Pods
dossier.scp_unleashed.131.caption: SCP-131-B, -C and -E during intake. They would not hold still for the camera.

page.title: Special Containment Procedures:
text: SCP-131 instances are free to roam the low-security corridors of their assigned site. For transport they may be carried by hand or kept in a standard containment locker, but they are happiest left free.
Corridors used by SCP-131 are to be kept free of open drops, deep water and lava. Staff are to watch their step around them.
**No instance of SCP-131 is to be harmed for any reason.** Staff who see an instance hurt are to report it at once.

page.title: Description:
text: SCP-131 is a group of six small creatures, each about 0.7 m tall and shaped like a teardrop with a thin tip that curls back over the body. Each has one large eye at the front, set behind a clear dome, and a pale base. The base hides a wheel, on which the instances move at up to 25 km/h.
The instances are coloured red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple, and are designated SCP-131-A to -F in that order. Each has its own voice: a short chirp, higher or lower than the others.
SCP-131 is curious and friendly. Instances follow staff they like, look up at them, race people who run and play with each other. They can be picked up and carried, and seem to enjoy it.
The instances are close to one another. When one is harmed, the rest react strongly.

page.title: Addendum 131-1: Behaviour Log
text: Agent R. reported that SCP-131-C followed him for the whole of a six hour shift, stopping when he stopped and looking up at him whenever he spoke.
Two instances that meet usually greet each other with a bump and a pair of chirps, then circle, chase or race one another before going their separate ways.
Sudden movement or a raised hand sends an instance zooming off. It keeps its distance from the person responsible for some time.

page.title: Addendum 131-2: Arrivals
page.text: SCP-131 has no recovery record. All six instances arrived together, zooming in from out of sight towards a researcher who had been reading this file. %rThey have done so again since.%r Their approach is always announced by chirping.

item.scp_unleashed.scp131_eye_pod.mood.h: It peers around, chirping now and then.
item.scp_unleashed.scp131_eye_pod.mood.s: It is quiet and keeps its eye down.
item.scp_unleashed.scp131_eye_pod.detail: Use it on a block to set it down again
Pick a pod up by using it with an empty hand
It keeps its colour, voice and name.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp131_eye_pod.1: SCP-131, the eye pods: small teardrop-shaped creatures with one large eye behind a glass dome and a wheel hidden in a pale base. They come in red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp131_eye_pod.2: They are curious and friendly. They zoom about, follow the people they like, play with each other and chirp, each in its own voice.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp131_eye_pod.3: Use a pod with an empty hand to pick it up and carry it. A carried pod keeps looking around. Use it on a block to set it down again.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp131_eye_pod.4: Eye pods cannot be crafted and never appear on their own. Read the SCP-131 dossier at an Archive Terminal.
jei.scp_unleashed.info.scp131_pod_spawn_: Spawns one eye pod in one of %s colours, picked at random.
Each pod has %s health, does not despawn and keeps its colour for good.
Operators can also use /scp_unleashed scp131 with spawn, family, grieve, cheer or status.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp131.unknown_co: Unknown colour "%s". Use red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp131.spawn.fail: There is no room for an eye pod here.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp131.family.suc: Spawned a family of %s eye pods.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp131.grieve.suc: The eye pods are grieving for %s seconds.
commands.scp_unleashed.scp131.status.gri: They are grieving for another %s seconds.
archive.scp_unleashed.notes.scp131.0: Listen for chirping. They come to you.
archive.scp_unleashed.notes.scp131.1: Be gentle with them. All of them.
